document.issued_by: nobody - the taxpayer's own records plus the charity's written acknowledgments

boxes.notes: Per-gift record (F-487). The i1040sca text reads: 'The written record must include the name of the charity, date, and amount of the contribution.' (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1040sca--2025.pdf).

boxes.label: Date of the contribution
boxes.notes: Per-gift record (F-487). The i1040sca text reads: 'The written record must include the name of the charity, date, and amount of the contribution.' (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1040sca--2025.pdf).

boxes.label: The gift was made in cash or by check (not property)
boxes.notes: Decides line 11 against line 12 for the item. The i1040sca text reads: 'Only enter on line 11 the deductible value of gifts you made in cash or by check.' (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1040sca--2025.pdf).

boxes.label: A contemporaneous written acknowledgment from the charity is held for this gift
boxes.notes: Each gift of $250 or more is tested separately; separate donations are not combined. The i1040sca text reads: 'You can deduct a gift of $250 or more only if you have a contemporaneous written acknowledgment from the charitable organization' (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1040sca--2025.pdf).

boxes.label: The donated property's value was determined by an appraisal
boxes.notes: Noncash gifts over $5,000 ($500 for certain clothing and household items). The i1040sca text reads: 'have to get appraisals of the values of the donated property.' (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1040sca--2025.pdf).

document.notes: A gift of $250 or more needs a contemporaneous written acknowledgment from the charity, and Form 8283 does not substitute for it. A noncash deduction over $500 requires Form 8283; over $5,000 generally requires an appraisal too. A contributed vehicle, boat or airplane is governed by its Form 1098-C, not by the taxpayer's estimate of value.

extraction.note: A taxpayer's own record. No prescribed layout, so no structured model and no boxes to read: it prints ITEMS in the client's own words, and which declared box each belongs in is a JUDGEMENT a person confirms (spec 075 group D, clarification Q1). Read by the declared custom model in TRANSCRIBE mode - the same reader, a second template - which copies every line verbatim and names no destination. A separate, cheap proposal call then suggests a box per item; **only a box a person confirms places anything**, so an engagement with nineteen rental sheets shows an empty Schedule E until somebody has looked. That is the decision, not a defect.
